notes: v4.1 CHELSA-native model: rebuilt PET/SPEI (Hargreaves-Samani, SPEI3/6 log-logistic, reference 1981-2010), temperature seasonality bio4 as SD x 100, 8 topographic layers, latitude as a non-increasing additive term (damps the north by design; the data cannot confirm or refute the northern increase). Label: catalogue x EFDA v3 (cat50 with +1 px buffer). Monotone XGBoost, isotonic calibration. Testing-period metrics, same convention as the other CHELSA-native models: trained on 1985-1997 and 80% of the 200 km tiles, tested on 2000-2020 in the other 20% of tiles (forward direction, the deployable one), mean of 5 spatial splits; the calibration was fitted on the training data only. AUC 0.886 (sd 0.040); cutoff 0.25: precision 0.49, recall 0.92, F1 0.62; cutoff 0.5: precision 0.65, recall 0.71, F1 0.67; best F1 0.68. Backward check (trained 2000-2020, tested 1985-1997): AUC 0.810, F1 0.57 at 0.25 and 0.60 at 0.5. These are case-control samples (26% positives in the forward test sample), so precision and recall do not describe real prevalence. Against EFDA v3 disturbance hits (spruce in the EFDA domain, 1985-2021, spatial holdout) the mean yearly AUC is 0.61: the maps rank where disturbance is more likely over the long term and do not track individual years. The layer value is a calibrated relative hazard index, not an outbreak probability. Futures are single climatological-normal snapshots (MPI-ESM1-2-HR), one GCM; SSP1-2.6 and SSP3-7.0 stand in for RCP2.6 and RCP4.5.
